discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele used a simple, transparent model of spin-orbit-coupled graphene to show that time-reversal-invariant insulators come in two distinct kinds. They identified a Z2 topological invariant that guarantees helical edge states protected against backscattering: the quantum spin Hall effect. This turned Berry-curvature ideas into a sharp, testable prediction. In 2007 Molenkamp's group realized that state in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, observing quantized edge conductance that appeared only above a critical well thickness, as band inversion requires. Theory and experiment then advanced together, as they must. The Z2 classification was generalized to three dimensions, leading to the discovery of surface Dirac fermions and later to the quantum anomalous Hall effect and topological classification of all band structures. Their work established topology as an organizing principle of electronic materials and set the agenda for hundreds of groups worldwide.
